newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends sharply lower, specs take profits.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends sharply lower, specs take profits.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures pulled back sharply in choppy dealings on Friday as speculators moved to take profits ahead of the weekend, traders said.
"It's Friday and it has been a volatile week," said Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes. "I think people were reluctant to hold their positions over the weekend."

Most-active May coffee ended down 4.55 cents at 161.85 cents a lb after ranging between 167.65 and 160.60 cents. Spot March coffee fell 3.65 cents to 174.80 cents, while the back months finished 0.85 to 5.05 lower.
The closely watched March/May switch widened to 12.95 cent, up from 12.05 cents at the close Thursday.
The market headed higher at the outset, in line with pre-opening expectations, but prices swung sharply on both sides of unchanged before caving in to speculative pressure.

Although there was little fresh fundmental input today, some traders said news Colombia and Mexico plan to boost annual consumption may have weighed on sentiment. But Merrill Lynch's Ganes countered that the plans were unlikely to have much impact on the supply situation any time soon.
"It won't affect anything for three years," she said, adding that their decision to increase out put was to be expected with the recent rise in futures.
A Mexican Coffee Council official said Friday the country plans to boost its annual coffee output to a total of about 8 million 60-kg bags by 2000 from a current output of 4.7 million bags.

Meanwhile, Colombia will seek to boost its coffee production to about 13 million bags in the coming years, the chief of Colombia's National Coffee Federation said. Jorge Cardenas told reporters ealier this week that out put was likely to come in at about 11 million bags this season.

Technically, traders said May's close beneath yesterday's low of 162.00 cents could lead to a test of near-term support at 160.00 cents. The next key downside target would be around 156.00-155.00, they said. On the upside, near-term resistance was seen at 168.50.
Volume on Friday reached an estimated 10,576 lots, down sharply from Thursday's official tally of 18,453 lots.

Traders in the options pit noted brisk sales of April 170.00 puts by commission houses. An estimated 4,033 lots of puts changed hands, while 1,972 lots of calls were traded. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodity Desk 212 859 1640))
